title: Image Smoother
statement: A grayscale picture is given as an `m x n` integer matrix `img`. Return a new matrix of the same shape in which every cell is replaced by its smoothed value: gather the cell itself plus each of its up to eight neighbours (horizontal, vertical or diagonal) that lie inside the picture, and take the integer average of those values, rounded down. Neighbours that would fall outside the grid are left out of both the sum and the count. All values are computed from the original `img`, not from cells already smoothed.
notes:
## Intuition

Each output cell depends only on a 3 x 3 window of the original picture, clipped at the borders. With at most nine cells per window, the simplest correct plan is to visit every cell, look at its window directly, and count only the neighbours that exist. Writing results into a separate matrix keeps the inputs untouched while we read them. (Prefix sums also work, but they buy nothing when the window is this small.)

## Approach

1. Read the dimensions into `rows` and `cols` and start an empty `result`.
2. For each cell `(r, c)`, reset `sum` and `count` to zero.
3. Try all nine offsets `dr`, `dc` in `-1..1`, giving the candidate `(nr, nc)`.
4. If the candidate is inside the grid, add `img[nr][nc]` to `sum` and increase `count`.
5. Push `Math.floor(sum / count)` into the current `row`; after the row is done, push it into `result`.

## Example 1, step by step

`img = [[1,1,1],[1,0,1],[1,1,1]]`. For the corner `(0, 0)` only four offsets stay inside: values `1, 1, 1, 0`, so `sum = 3`, `count = 4` and `floor(0.75) = 0`. For the edge cell `(0, 1)` six cells qualify, `sum = 5`, `count = 6`, giving `0`. The centre sees all nine, `sum = 8`, `count = 9`, giving `0`. Every cell becomes `0`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(m·n): each cell inspects at most nine positions.
- Space: O(m·n) for the returned matrix, O(1) extra besides it.

## Pitfalls

- Divide by the number of cells actually inside the grid, not always by 9.
- Do not write smoothed values back into `img` while you are still reading neighbours from it.
- Round down: `Math.floor` (or integer division in Java and C), never rounding to nearest.
- A single row or single column has no diagonal neighbours on one side; the bounds check handles it.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `rows`, `cols` | dimensions of `img` |
| `result` | the smoothed picture being built |
| `r`, `c` | the cell being smoothed |
| `row` | smoothed values of row `r` so far |
| `sum`, `count` | total and number of in-grid cells in the window |
| `dr`, `dc` | offsets from `-1` to `1` |
| `nr`, `nc` | the neighbour position being tried |

narration.2: Remember how many rows the picture has.
narration.3: Remember how many columns each row has.
narration.6: Visit every row of the picture.
narration.8: Visit every cell of the current row.
narration.9: Start the window total at zero for this cell.
narration.10: No cells of the window have been counted yet.
narration.11: Try the row above, the same row and the row below.
narration.12: Try the column to the left, the same column and the column to the right.
narration.15: Only use the neighbour if it lies inside the picture.
narration.16: Add its value to the window total.
narration.17: Count it so the average divides by the right number.
narration.21: Store the average of the window, rounded down.
narration.23: The row is finished; add it to the result.
narration.25: Every cell is smoothed; return the new picture.
